title: Agent導入後の負債蓄積速度は、AI設定をRepositoryにCommitしているかで約2倍変わる
summary: Coding agent導入によるCommit量増加(28-38%)は設定の有無に関わらず得られる一方、品質コストは分岐する。AI設定をVersion管理していないRepositoryではCognitive complexityが約53%増、静的解析警告が1.7倍に増えたのに対し、Commit済み設定があるRepositoryでは複雑度増加が約27%に留まった。つまりE10の「生成量に比例した負債蓄積」は無条件ではなく、AI設定のVersion管理という具体的な調整変数を持つ。441 Repositoryの観察研究であり因果ではない点に注意が必要。

evidence.title: A Few Pages of Markdown: Committed AI Configuration and Lower Quality Cost after Coding-Agent Adoption
evidence.summary: Introduces RAMP (Repository AI Maturity Profile), a four-level cumulative maturity model over version-controlled artifacts, across 441 repositories, validated against independent human annotation at 97% accuracy on held-out samples. Velocity rose 28-38% in commits at all maturity levels; cognitive complexity rose ~53% with static-analysis warnings 1.7x without committed AI configuration, versus ~27% with it.

notes: Not a new problem: E10 already states that technical debt accumulates faster in proportion to AI generation volume. Material change is the quantified moderator - committed AI configuration roughly halves the complexity increase at equal velocity gain - which promotes 'commit your AI configuration' from D-category hygiene to a measured E10 mitigation and gives the catalog a concrete metric pair (cognitive complexity, static-analysis warning rate) for monitoring. Also relevant to D04/D12 as counter-evidence that configuration files are not merely instruction debt. Observational design, so association not causation.
